// why: One job: catch a name that no longer exists.
public/ is plain classic <script> JS sharing one global scope, deliberately
(see tsconfig.json). Nothing checked it, so a variable renamed in one file
kept parsing everywhere else and only threw when the line was finally
reached — three times so far: gridViewerCount after the Vue migration,
allProjects after getProjectSets collapsed two fetches into one, and
renderPlans, which survives only because App.vue assigns it to window.
This config is NOT a type-checking pass and must not become one. Running it
reports a few hundred type complaints the renderer has no interest in;
test/renderer-globals.test.js runs it and reads only the undefined-name
codes, TS2304 and TS2552. Everything else is ignored on purpose.
